users.description: One row per user. MVP has exactly one seeded row ('user'), but the shape supports more.

password_hash.description: Salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash, stored as 'salt$digest' in one column.

boards.description: One row per user's board. MVP: exactly one board per user.

user_id.description: UNIQUE enforces one-board-per-user as a real DB constraint, not just app logic.

board_columns.description: The 5 fixed columns of a board (To Do, In Progress, Review, Blocked, Done). Never added or removed after seeding, only renamed.

id.description: e.g. 'col-1' .. 'col-5', matching the frontend's existing id scheme.

position.description: 0-4, fixed column order. SQLite does not guarantee row order, and column order is meaningful to the UI, so it must be stored explicitly.

cards.description: Kanban cards. A flat table (not nested under columns), matching the frontend's CardData shape exactly.

due_date.description: ISO date 'YYYY-MM-DD', or NULL. Matches the frontend's `string | null` exactly — no conversion needed either direction.

position.description: Order within its column. Recomputed (only for the affected column(s)) on every add/move/delete, mirroring the frontend reducer's existing MOVE_CARD splice logic.

indexes.note: Not created for the MVP — a handful of rows per user does not need them. If this ever supports many users/cards, add indexes on board_columns.board_id and cards.column_id.

seed_data.description: On first run (empty DB), the seeded 'user' gets one board with the same 5 columns and 8 dummy cards currently hardcoded in frontend/src/lib/seed-data.ts, so the app's out-of-the-box experience is unchanged.
